content.overview: A culture is not production-ready because shoots multiplied or roots appeared. Release evidence must cover functional transition, identity, morphology, passage history and defined quality limits.

vocabulary.definition: Progressive adaptation from in-vitro conditions to conventional substrate and environment.
The documented sequence and count of culture transfers for a line.

sections.title: Rooting and acclimation form one transition
sections.body: Plantlets leaving culture face a different water, light, airflow and root-function environment. Survival and new growth over time matter more than root presence alone.

sections.title: Fidelity uses multiple evidence streams
sections.body: Identity records, passage history, morphology, performance and justified molecular or cytometric tests provide complementary evidence. No single check proves complete stability.

sections.title: Release criteria must be explicit
sections.body: A release packet should identify stage, survival window, growth response, identity continuity, exceptions, reviewer and limitations. Material that misses a criterion follows hold, investigation or disposition rules.

workedExamples: Plantlets with visible roots but repeated collapse after transfer have not met an establishment criterion.
Normal appearance after many passages does not erase the need to retain passage and route history.
commonMistakes: Defining success at first visible root.
Using appearance as the only fidelity check.
Releasing a partial batch without recording exclusions and denominator changes.
content.practicalApplication: Build a release packet for a mock line containing identity, passage, rooting, acclimation survival, new-growth, morphology, exceptions and an authorized status decision.
content.summary: Clean-stock release follows the material through functional acclimation and preserves identity, history, quality evidence and decision authority.
